semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2 requires the swarm to continuously operate within its state areas, which are owned by UAVSwarmStateMachine. The exact closed transition inventory (fcstm_model.text lines 2-10, 40) shows the only root-level initial edge is transition:line:40 '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial', a synthetic leaf with zero outgoing transitions; UAVSwarmStateMachine and all its descendants are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts and refuted in verify_facts. This is a complete-inventory absence of the required owner-local default-entry edge into UAVSwarmStateMachine, decidable from the exact source/target/scope endpoints without needing a dedicated predicate. The proposed local-nested-edge rebuttal addresses a different, owner-local well-formedness property (SearchRegion/MissionRegion local entry) and does not establish a root-to-UAVSwarmStateMachine path; per the initial-entry scope protocol, a separate valid nested/local edge does not rebut this owner-local root-entry defect, so the defeater is defeated.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: Nested initial edges exist locally inside SearchRegion ([*] -> Idle) and MissionRegion ([*] -> MissionActive) and are individually well-formed, so one might argue local entry suffices.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The root machine's initial pseudostate edge must enter UAVSwarmStateMachine (or an equivalent default-entry chain reaching it) so the swarm's continuous target-search operation is structurally reachable.

additional_contracts.normative_statement: The UAV swarm's target-search mission operating scope (UAVSwarmStateMachine) must be reachable from the closed model's top-level initial entry so that the described continuous target-search behavior across its state areas can actually execute.
additional_contracts.quote: Before the mission is completed, the UAV swarm continuously performs target search tasks, during which it operates within three different state areas.
additional_contracts.reason: NL2 requires the UAV swarm to continuously operate across three state areas before mission completion, which presupposes that the enclosing operating scope owning those areas (UAVSwarmStateMachine) is itself reachable from the closed model's top-level initial entry. The closed FCSTM instead routes the root initial edge only to a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf with no outgoing transition, leaving the entire UAVSwarmStateMachine subtree (and thus every state area, transition, and consumer inside it) structurally unreachable. This is a distinct root-reachability property from the local initial_entry edges nested inside SearchRegion/MissionRegion, which do exist and correctly target Idle/MissionActive respectively.
additional_contracts.scope: UAV swarm mission operating scope, root reachability

response.reason: The closed FCSTM root only reaches UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic dead-end leaf); the entire UAVSwarmStateMachine subtree (SearchRegion, MissionRegion, and all their child states) is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability, states[].reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts reachability checks (all refuted except UnspecifiedInitial). This root-level defect causes every NL2-4 obligation located inside UAVSwarmStateMachine to fail operationally even though the local transition edges, guards, and effects exist as authored. I audit root reachability, consumer coverage, and termination consequences distinctly: (1) the whole operating scope is unreachable from root, justifying one derived reachability contract on UAVSwarmStateMachine; (2) both event-consumer-coverage contracts (Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received) have zero reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[].reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and verify_facts event_consumer checks all status=refuted; (3) the two transition_endpoints contracts (NL3, NL4) have their exact source/target edges present in the closed model (Searching->FormationAdjustment on Intercepted at transition:line:18; Searching->Attacking on Task_Assignment_Received at transition:line:19) so I do not raise wrong_target on those, but I flag the derived reachability/consumer defects that make these edges operationally inert; (4) the NL2 cardinality/state_action/containment contracts are structural, primarily owned by the other lens, but the state_action (continuous target-search) contract also suffers a consequence: Searching is unreachable so the required continuous progress obligation cannot execute -- however per instructions this is routed as an initial_entry/reachability defect rather than duplicated deadlock claim since Searching has exact outgoing continuation (not a leaf); (5) NL4-VARIABLE-1 (variable_delta on attack exit) is unaffected in its local carrier (transition:line:21 exists with no effect field) — I leave that to the sibling lens since it is a local carrier-content issue, not a behavioral-consequence property, but note here only the reachability consequence. I add one additional_contracts row for root reachability of UAVSwarmStateMachine since no supplied contract states that exact scope-level obligation, deriving it from NL2's mission-operating-scope semantics (the mission necessarily requires the swarm to operate in this scope).

Obligations i0, i5, i6 concern the same core defect: the closed model's only root-level initial edge targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf with zero outgoing transitions, leaving UAVSwarmStateMachine and all of its descendants unreachable from the model root. i5 and i6 are backed by an exact G1 (may_reach) predicate: i6 has a completed backend receipt with verdict=false and an explicit counterexample confirming unreachability, so it is established with no competent defeater (the sibling nested initial edges are a different, owner-local property and do not rebut root-level unreachability). i5 has the same exact G1 binding but was not executed by a sound backend (predicate-null/backend-unsupported), yet the same deterministic inspection/verify facts (reachable_from_initial=false, refuted checks) already establish the identical unreachability fact independent of the missing backend run, so it is established as well, per the D boundary rule that predicate-null status does not erase a precise issue confirmed by exact supplied facts. i0 restates the same defect at the initial-entry/source level (missing owner-local default-entry edge into UAVSwarmStateMachine); the exact transition inventory (only transition:line:40 as root initial edge, targeting UnspecifiedInitial) and the reachability facts establish this absence directly; the proposed rebuttal (local nested initial edges into SearchRegion/MissionRegion) is a different, owner-local property that does not rebut root-to-UAVSwarmStateMachine reachability, so it is defeated.

i1-i4 and i7 concern event-consumer coverage for the Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received, and aggregate scope events. In each case, inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows a declared consumer transition (authored correctly, matching NL text) but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty, and verify_facts marks the corresponding check as refuted. This is a distinct property from transition endpoint correctness or upstream reachability, per the frontier discipline: a declared but unreachable consumer does not satisfy the exact reachable-consumer-coverage obligation, even though the transition's own event/target binding is well-formed. The proposed rebuttal in each case (the transition is well-formed; unreachability stems from the separate root-entry defect) is a different property and does not rebut the exact reachable-consumer-coverage claim, so it is defeated; grounding is established for i1, i2, i3, i4, i7.

i8 and i9 are deterministic cardinality/containment frontier checks that were explicitly retained as unresolved because no binding/grounding lens could select one exact primary member domain, owner, or child state identity; element_refs are empty and binding_status=identity_unresolved. This is a genuine dossier-level indecision (not merely predicate/backend unavailability dressed as ambiguity) since the binding itself never resolved to an exact model identity, so grounding=unresolved for both, with no defeater since no competent alternative reading has been supplied (defeater_kind=none, disposition=unresolved-consistent, i.e., left as unresolved with no surviving defeater asserted).

semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2 requires the swarm to continuously operate within its state areas, which are owned by UAVSwarmStateMachine. The exact closed transition inventory (fcstm_model.text lines 2-10, 40) shows the only root-level initial edge is transition:line:40 '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial', a synthetic leaf with zero outgoing transitions; UAVSwarmStateMachine and all its descendants are reachable_from_initial=false in inspection_equivalent_facts and refuted in verify_facts. This is a complete-inventory absence of the required owner-local default-entry edge into UAVSwarmStateMachine, decidable from the exact source/target/scope endpoints without needing a dedicated predicate. The proposed local-nested-edge rebuttal addresses a different, owner-local well-formedness property (SearchRegion/MissionRegion local entry) and does not establish a root-to-UAVSwarmStateMachine path; per the initial-entry scope protocol, a separate valid nested/local edge does not rebut this owner-local root-entry defect, so the defeater is defeated.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: Nested initial edges exist locally inside SearchRegion ([*] -> Idle) and MissionRegion ([*] -> MissionActive) and are individually well-formed, so one might argue local entry suffices.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The root machine's initial pseudostate edge must enter UAVSwarmStateMachine (or an equivalent default-entry chain reaching it) so the swarm's continuous target-search operation is structurally reachable.

cardinality_bindings.reason: This behavior_consequence lens focuses on reachability and consumer-coverage consequences rather than the structural region/state-area domain decision; it does not have a distinct exact reading beyond what the complementary structural lens would supply, and no owner_model_ref is bound here to avoid duplicating or overriding the primary structural lens's domain selection.

branches.reason: The closed FCSTM root only reaches UnspecifiedInitial (a synthetic dead-end leaf); the entire UAVSwarmStateMachine subtree (SearchRegion, MissionRegion, and all their child states) is unreachable from the top-level initial entry per inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability, states[].reachable_from_initial=false, and verify_facts reachability checks (all refuted except UnspecifiedInitial). This root-level defect causes every NL2-4 obligation located inside UAVSwarmStateMachine to fail operationally even though the local transition edges, guards, and effects exist as authored. I audit root reachability, consumer coverage, and termination consequences distinctly: (1) the whole operating scope is unreachable from root, justifying one derived reachability contract on UAVSwarmStateMachine; (2) both event-consumer-coverage contracts (Intercepted, Task_Assignment_Received) have zero reachable consumers per inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[].reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] and verify_facts event_consumer checks all status=refuted; (3) the two transition_endpoints contracts (NL3, NL4) have their exact source/target edges present in the closed model (Searching->FormationAdjustment on Intercepted at transition:line:18; Searching->Attacking on Task_Assignment_Received at transition:line:19) so I do not raise wrong_target on those, but I flag the derived reachability/consumer defects that make these edges operationally inert; (4) the NL2 cardinality/state_action/containment contracts are structural, primarily owned by the other lens, but the state_action (continuous target-search) contract also suffers a consequence: Searching is unreachable so the required continuous progress obligation cannot execute -- however per instructions this is routed as an initial_entry/reachability defect rather than duplicated deadlock claim since Searching has exact outgoing continuation (not a leaf); (5) NL4-VARIABLE-1 (variable_delta on attack exit) is unaffected in its local carrier (transition:line:21 exists with no effect field) — I leave that to the sibling lens since it is a local carrier-content issue, not a behavioral-consequence property, but note here only the reachability consequence. I add one additional_contracts row for root reachability of UAVSwarmStateMachine since no supplied contract states that exact scope-level obligation, deriving it from NL2's mission-operating-scope semantics (the mission necessarily requires the swarm to operate in this scope).

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 is purely descriptive/introductory (title/domain statement) and establishes no independently violable obligation, so it is marked context. NL2 yields two independent obligations: a cardinality obligation over 'three state areas' (kept unresolved member_domain since NL does not establish concurrent-region or direct-child-state semantics explicitly) and a continuous state_action obligation for the target search task, per the rule that explicit continuous/repeated tasks get independent state_action contracts even alongside cardinality obligations in the same segment. NL3 yields one transition endpoint contract from the continuing mission-operating scope to the formation adjustment state, with the interception condition preserved as an event hint on the endpoint rather than a separate guard contract, since it only selects/triggers the transition. NL4 yields two independent obligations: the flight-to-attack transition endpoint (with the task-assignment-received condition as an event hint), and a separate variable_delta obligation for the UAV count decrease effect tied to attack completion, kept as its own contract because effects are independent from endpoint existence per the shape rules. No termination contract is manufactured for 'mission completed' since NL2 only says 'before the mission is completed' without establishing an explicit ending state or endpoint requiring termination semantics; this remains a temporal qualifier, not a termination target. No transition_groups were created because no segment establishes a genuine shared-source multi-alternative branch group; NL3 and NL4 each describe a single-target transition from a resolved source, not coordinated alternatives.
